notable_absence.predicate: hasInternalComponent / offersConfigurationChoice (imprecise fit for two rows)
notable_absence.finding: Two rows resist clean modeling. (1) 'Index Replicas' states a placement constraint on WHERE a replica may live ('Replicas exist on nodes separate from the current active replica or any other replicas') rather than a per-node configuration value, so configuredPerNode is a loose fit - the registry's closest real match (requiresDedicatedNode) is about services, not index replicas, so I used configuredPerNode as the least-wrong available predicate and am flagging the mismatch rather than forcing a better-sounding one. (2) The table itself is a flat list of unrelated settings (scoring, defaults, dynamic-field storage, replicas, index type, partitions) with no stated grouping predicate - I did not mint a 'hasSetting' or 'offersAdvancedSetting' predicate to link search:set-advanced-settings to each option as a component, because the page's own structure is a UI form, not a stated part-whole claim, and hasInternalComponent is reserved (per its own definition) for real component concepts, not arbitrary form fields.

cross_component_finding: MOST IMPORTANT FINDING OF THIS PAGE: create-custom-analyzer.json (earlier in this batch) asserted search:full-text-index -configurableVia-> search:custom-analyzer from the sentence 'you can set it as the default analyzer ... for your Search index.' This page's own Advanced Settings table is more precise about WHERE that default lives: 'Change the default analyzer assigned to type mappings in the index' - the default analyzer is a property of a TYPE MAPPING (search:type-mapping), not the index as a flat whole. I recorded the more precise relation here (search:type-mapping -configurableVia-> search:custom-analyzer) alongside, not instead of, the coarser one already on disk, since both are independently true statements from two different pages and only reconciliation should decide whether the coarser one should be narrowed or kept as a valid looser paraphrase. The same refinement likely applies to the Default Date/Time Parser row, which this page states at the index level ('used for date data in your documents') consistent with the sibling batch's search:full-text-index -hasInternalComponent-> search:date-time-parser - so date/time parser and analyzer defaults are NOT symmetric: one is index-scoped, the other (per this page's own wording) is type-mapping-scoped, even though both are configured from the same Advanced Settings form.
cross_product_finding: search:scoring-model was minted independently on the Capella side (cloud/search/customize-index.json, cloud/search/search-index-params.json, cloud/search/run-searches.json) from wording nearly identical to this server page's Scoring Model row - both say 'Couchbase Server version 8.0 ... Choose the specific scoring model you want to use for scoring search results for this Search index: tf-idf ... bm25'. This page was not among the round's eight pre-flagged filename-identical pairs (set-advanced-settings.md has no measured Capella twin comparison in this round's dispatch), but the Scoring Model content itself is genuinely shared verbatim wording across cloud/ and server/8.0/, now corroborated a sixth time by this record - real content on both sides, so this finding is reported rather than skipped, per the evidence-gate rule that a cross_product_finding fires only where there is real content on both sides to compare (which there is here, discovered independently of the pre-flagged list).
